figura.config.wonkyplugin.tooltip: Heh, you could say the plugin's a bit wonky...
figura.config.net_allowed_ports.tooltip: Defines which ports should be allowed in NetAPI and WebSockets
figura.docs.wonky.get_bumpscocity: Gets the Narrator to rate the current bumpscocity (requires SillyPlugin)
figura.docs.websocket: A global API that contains WebSocket related features
figura.docs.websocket.connect:
Opens a WebSocket connection to an address
Must use ws:// or wss:// protocols
figura.docs.websocket.poll: Polls the socket, returning data up to a newline, or nil if there is no new data
figura.docs.websocket.has_message: Returns true if there is any available data in the buffer
figura.docs.websocket.is_closed: Returns true if this socket is closed
figura.docs.websocket.has_error: Returns true if this socket was closed due to an error
figura.docs.websocket.get_close_code: Returns the numerical close code for this socket, or -1 if it isn't closed
figura.docs.websocket.get_close_reason: Returns the textual close reason for this socket, or the empty string if it isn't closed
figura.docs.websocket.get_uri:
Returns the socket's URI
Useful for checking what socket an event belongs to
figura.docs.websocket.get_open_sockets: Returns a table containing all sockets that haven't explicitly been closed
figura.docs.events.websocket_data:
This event runs when a WebSocket receives data
The first parameter is the socket itself
The second parameter is the data received
figura.docs.events.websocket_closed:
This event runs when a WebSocket closes
The first parameter is the socket itself
The second parameter is true if it was closed due to an error
The third parameter is the textual close reason
The fourth parameter is the numerical close code
figura.docs.wonky.match_regex:
Returns all matches of a string against a regular expression
Returns three tables: "matches", "groups" (numbered), "names" (named groups)
Capture groups only return the last match   
Use Java embedded flag syntax to set flags, for example "(?i)" for case insensitive matching
Don't forget to escape backslash metacharacters (\d -> \\d)
figura.docs.wonky.replace_regex:
Replaces all matches of a string against a regex with another string
Use Java embedded flag syntax to set flags, for example "(?i)" for case insensitive matching
Don't forget to escape backslash metacharacters (\d -> \\d)
wonkyplugin.permissions.value.print_json: Whether or not the player can print arbitrary JSON text.
